title: Uniform and Harbor
premise: In the port city of Vellham, on the eve of revolution, Juniper Fairweather cuts typefaces in her father's print shop, keeping her head down as census takers catalog the city for a regime tightening its grip. When an over-curious census taker, Elias Marren, uncovers that her late mother's records were falsified to hide a forbidden lineage, Juniper realizes the regime plans to erase entire families from the official record before the history books are written. Risking everything, she partners with Elias—whose duty and conscience war within him—to print the true census, with the names the victors want struck out, before the archives are sealed. The book ends with Juniper distributing the forbidden pages through the harbor as the city rises, choosing to be seen at last, her name and her mother's set in lead and ink.
about_author: Juniper Sterling is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade restoring water-damaged municipal records from coastal cities. Her fiction is drawn from the marginalia, crossed-out names, and unsent letters she found in the ledgers no one was meant to read.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She sorts movable type in her father's print shop, establishing the rhythm of her careful, invisible life in Vellham. When soldiers post new census edicts, her father quietly removes a name from a printed list. Emotional beat: the comfort of smallness, and the first crack in it.

chapters.title: Questions in the Doorway
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Census taker Elias Marren arrives to update the household register and asks about her mother, dead twelve years, whose entry is oddly blank. Juniper deflects, but his pen lingers. Emotional beat: unease—the sense of being measured for the first time.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Forgot
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Searching her mother's belongings for the census follow-up, she finds a locket key and a torn half-page in a hand she doesn't recognize. Her father burns papers at night. Emotional beat: the discovery that invisibility was engineered, not natural.

chapters.title: The Taker's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. At the census bureau, Elias notices the Fairweather file has been flagged for 'correction'—a euphemism he's beginning to understand. His superior, Director Hale, praises his thoroughness. Emotional beat: a dutiful man feels the first tremor of complicity.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Nails
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A harbor printer named Sable, an old friend of her mother's, recognizes the torn half-page as proof of a purged family registry. She warns Juniper that flagged households vanish before the archives close. Emotional beat: grief curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: The Second Visit
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Ordered to 'complete' the Fairweather record, Elias returns and finds Juniper waiting with questions of her own. They strike an uneasy truce: she'll answer, if he shows her what the corrections mean. Emotional beat: two careful people recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Room of Red Strings
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias sneaks into the bureau's correction room and sees the scale of the erasure—hundreds of names struck, whole streets rewritten. He copies one page, hands shaking. Emotional beat: duty fractures; he can no longer claim ignorance.

chapters.title: The Key and the Cellar
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The locket key opens a cellar cache beneath the print shop: her mother's hidden press plates and a full, true census from the last purge. Her father confesses he printed it and let her mother take the blame. Emotional beat: betrayal and inheritance in one breath.

chapters.title: Salt on the Wind
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Rumors of revolution reach the harbor; sailors strike, and soldiers seal the customs house. Sable urges printing the true census now, before the victors' historians arrive to sanitize everything. Emotional beat: the clock starts ticking in earnest.

chapters.title: A Debt in Duplicate
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Hale discovers a missing page and begins hunting the leak. Elias, under suspicion, must report Juniper or protect her. He delivers a falsified report instead, crossing a line he cannot uncross. Emotional beat: terror braided with resolve.

chapters.title: The Typesetter's Vow
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Father and daughter reconcile over the old press plates; he teaches her the locked case of rare characters her mother designed. They begin setting the true census by candlelight. Emotional beat: love expressed as shared labor, forgiveness in lead type.

chapters.title: Harbor of the Unrecorded
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She gathers testimonies from families on the purge list—the fishwife, the lighthouse keeper, the drowned boy's mother—each name a small act of defiance. Emotional beat: the erased become a chorus; belonging found among the uncounted.

chapters.title: Hale's Net
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Hale raids Sable's dockside print room and arrests two printers. Elias realizes his forged report bought days, not safety. He warns Sable's network through a coded shipping notice. Emotional beat: the hunter's machinery closing in, and him inside it.

chapters.title: What Cannot Be Carried
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. With soldiers quartering nearby, the family must decide what to save—the press plates or the testimony pages. Juniper chooses the names; her father, the type. They hide the plates in the harbor's coal barges. Emotional beat: sacrifice measured in what's left behind.

chapters.title: The Interrogation of Elias Marren
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Hale confronts Elias with the coded notice; Elias deflects by offering a credible false suspect, damning an innocent clerk. He despises what survival is making him. Emotional beat: the cost of loyalty to a corrupted duty.

chapters.title: Midnight Impression
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The true census is printed—three hundred copies—in a single night run while the city burns barricades at its edges. The press breaks on the last signature: her mother's name. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by the unfinished.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Customs House
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The clerk Elias sacrificed turns out to be Sable's cousin, and the network turns on Elias. Juniper must vouch for him before Sable's people, staking her credibility on a man who lied to everyone, including her. Emotional beat: trust as a wager, not a gift.

chapters.title: The Sealing of the Archives
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Hale announces the archives close in three days; after that, only the victors' version will exist. Elias steals the master purge order naming every corrected household. Emotional beat: a man finally choosing truth over uniform.

chapters.title: Smoke Over Vellham
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Revolution ignites fully; the print shop is torched by a regime squad hunting the census copies. Juniper and Elias escape through the coal barges with the plates and the purge order, her father wounded. Emotional beat: loss and flight, the past literally burning.

chapters.title: The Long Dock
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At the harbor, the network loads the true census onto fishing boats bound for cities the regime can't reach, while Hale's soldiers sweep the docks. Juniper sets her mother's name in type at last, repairing the broken signature by lantern light. Emotional beat: grief completed into monument.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Names
chapters.summary: Juniper's and Elias's POVs alternating. As the regime falls in the streets, Juniper reads the true census aloud from the customs house steps while Elias surrenders the purge order to the crowd, accepting judgment for his years as a taker. Emotional beat: climax—truth spoken before the victors can rewrite it; accountability embraced.

chapters.title: Set in Permanent Type
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, one year later. The rebuilt print shop prints the city's new register—every name restored, Elias now its archivist, Hale tried by the people's tribunal. Juniper cuts a new typeface in her mother's style and signs the first edition. Emotional beat: resolution—belonging chosen, truth on the record, love and duty reconciled.
